On the Bakhshālī Manuscript

By A. F. Rudolf Hoernle (Vienna, 1887)

A. F. Rudolf Hoernle

Hoernle’s first account of the Bakhshālī manuscript, the birch-bark arithmetic found in 1881 in north-western India, with its rules, its notation and the early use of a zero (Vienna, 1887).

docs.text:
Hoernle’s first account of the Bakhshālī manuscript, the birch-bark arithmetic found in 1881 in north-western India, with its rules, its notation and the early use of a zero (Vienna, 1887). Listed in the catalogue of the Rare Book Society of India.

From Internet Archive · Public domain in India

Scanned from a copy in the Gerstein Science Information Centre, University of Toronto; hosted by the Internet Archive. Item: On the Bakshali manuscript · Hoernle, August Frederich Rudolf, 1841-1918 · 1887, 32 scanned pages. Published 1887; A. F. Rudolf Hoernle died 1918; the manuscript is ancient; public domain in India.

This book is not stored in this library: its pages are shown from the Internet Archive when they are opened, in this library's own viewer, and each chapter ends with this credit. The pages are shown as scans in this library's viewer (zoom, pan, thumbnails); the machine reading of these scans is not good enough to be shown as text.
